dcf.method: 5-year FCFF: EBITDA - tax on EBIT - capex - change in net working capital; growth fades linearly from the starting rate to the year-5 rate; Gordon terminal value; equity = EV - borrowings.

blocks.text: [F] Fluidomat makes fixed-speed and variable-speed hydrodynamic fluid couplings. These are the devices placed between a motor and a driven machine (conveyor, crusher, fan, boiler-feed pump, mill) that allow a soft start and protect against overload; the variable-speed versions also control speed (AR2025 p.87; PPT Jun 2026). [F] It reports a single segment, 'manufacturing of fluid couplings' (AR2025 p.38, p.89). [F] Revenue is almost entirely product sales: in FY25, Rs 71.53 cr of the Rs 72.18 cr revenue from operations was 'sale of products (including spares & components)', Rs 0.59 cr was services and Rs 0.06 cr scrap (AR2025 p.99).

[F] All manufacturing is at one plant in Dewas, Madhya Pradesh. The plant has aluminium and cast-iron foundries, CNC machining, fabrication and ten test benches (AR2025 p.68; PPT Jun 2026). [F] There were 200 permanent employees at 31 March 2025 (AR2025 p.35). [MC] Management names power, refinery and oil & gas, cement, mining, steel, material handling, chemicals and fertiliser, off-highway and marine as end markets (PPT Jun 2026). [F] No revenue split by end market, product family or customer is disclosed anywhere in the documents (AR2025 p.38; PPT Jun 2026). [F] The only geographic data point is export earnings: Rs 2.19 cr in FY25, down from Rs 2.79 cr in FY24 (AR2025 p.46, p.102). [E] That is about 3.0% of FY25 revenue, against 5.0% in FY24, so roughly 97% of sales are domestic.

[MC] Management says the customer base is more than 600 industrial clients and names NTPC, Coal India, ONGC, BPCL, HPCL and Adani as key clients (PPT Jun 2026). [MC] It also cites refinery case studies at BPCL Bina, MRPL, Numaligarh Refinery, IOCL Barauni and Petronas Malaysia (PPT Jun 2026). [AI] From these names, the customer profile looks like public-sector utilities and refiners plus EPC contractors and heavy-industry owners. Revenue per customer is not disclosed, so concentration cannot be measured.

**Evidence-base caveat.** [F] Our statements data covers FY19 to FY23 only, with the latest quarter at March 2023 (NUMBERS). [F] The company's own documents run to FY26 (March 2026): the audited FY25 annual report and an unaudited FY26 investor presentation dated 29 June 2026 (AR2025 p.83-85; PPT Jun 2026). [F] The FY26 annual report was filed on 2 September 2026 and the Q1 FY27 results were published on 15 August 2026, but neither document was available to us (ANNOUNCEMENTS). [AI] Every valuation metric and DCF in this report rests on the March 2023 base. Company-reported revenue has since risen from Rs 45.41 cr to Rs 72.46 cr, so the model inputs are stale, and we flag this wherever it matters.

[F] Listing status: the company is an established BSE listing (scrip 522017), not a recent IPO (AR2025 p.67). [F] Its CIN, L74210MP1978PLC001452, records a 1978 registration (AR2025 p.9). [MC] Management and the screener profile give 1971 as the founding year (SCREENER; PPT Jun 2026). [AI] No prospectus was available. There are no IPO lock-ins or use-of-proceeds issues to track.

subsections.title: Bear thesis: reasons not to own it

items: 1. **Growth has stalled.** [F] FY26 revenue was Rs 72.46 cr against Rs 72.18 cr in FY25, flat, and PAT fell from Rs 22.22 cr to Rs 20.06 cr (PPT Jun 2026). [E] Read from the chart, Q4 FY26 revenue was about Rs 21 cr against about Rs 29 cr in Q4 FY25, and quarterly EPS fell from Rs 20.8 to Rs 13.0 (PPT Jun 2026).

2. **Order intake has been below sales.** [F] Orders booked in FY25 were Rs 58.16 cr, down 3.1% from Rs 60.03 cr in FY24 (AR2025 p.27). [E] FY25 book-to-bill was therefore about 0.81x, against about 1.08x in FY24. That pattern is consistent with the backlog being drawn down to reach FY25 revenue, followed by a flat FY26.

3. **Receivables are growing much faster than sales.** [F] Trade receivables rose from Rs 13.47 cr (March 2024) to Rs 22.46 cr (March 2025) and Rs 29.63 cr (March 2026) (AR2025 p.83; PPT Jun 2026). [E] Debtor days on revenue went from about 89 to 114 to 149. [F] Operating cash flow was Rs 14.30 cr against PAT of Rs 22.22 cr in FY25 (AR2025 p.85).

4. **Valuation is far above every DCF scenario.** [F] At Rs 750, the price is above the bull-case value of Rs 178.4 per share, and the reverse DCF implies about 86% annual sales growth for five years (NUMBERS). [AI] The model's base is stale and its 19% margin is conservative, but even allowing for that, the gap is large.

5. **FY25 margins may have been a peak.** [F] Management itself calls FY26 a 'normalisation of margins from the elevated levels of FY25', attributed to product and customer mix and input cost pressure (PPT Jun 2026). [E] Operating EBITDA margin moved from about 26.8% (FY24) to 37.8% (FY25) and about 33.0% (FY26).

6. **Exports are small and shrinking despite the 'global footprint' pitch.** [F] Export earnings fell from Rs 2.79 cr to Rs 2.19 cr in FY25 (AR2025 p.46). [MC] The presentation says the company exports to '15+ countries' (PPT Jun 2026).

7. **Family-run governance with rising pay.** [F] Three promoter-family executive directors were paid Rs 2.49 cr in FY25 [E, about 11% of PAT]. Four more relatives or family members sit in senior roles, among them the CFO and the heads of marketing and international business (AR2025 p.35, p.52, p.104). [F] Shareholders were asked to raise pay caps and to approve pay above the 5%-of-net-profit threshold for promoter executives (AR2025 p.5-8).

8. **Disclosure quality is inconsistent.** [F] The P&L reports EPS of Rs 45.15, while the EPS note computes Rs 45.10 on PAT and shows Rs 45.15 only after adding other comprehensive income. For FY24 the figures are Rs 28.23 against Rs 26.50 (AR2025 p.84, p.102). [F] CSR spend is given as Rs 19.95 lakh in one place and Rs 25.15 lakh in another (AR2025 p.33, p.44). [F] R&D expenditure is reported as NIL, although the presentation cites 'continuous R&D' (AR2025 p.46; PPT Jun 2026).

9. **Cyclical, lumpy, public-sector-linked demand.** [MC] Growth is tied to thermal power, coal mining and refinery projects (AR2025 p.36). [F] The company had to file an insolvency petition against BGR Energy Systems in 2022 to recover dues; it settled in October 2024 (AR2025 p.38-39).
10. **Single site, rising capital intensity.** [F] All production is in Dewas (AR2025 p.68). [MC] The Rs 35 cr capex is about 1.4x the FY25 gross block of Rs 25.10 cr [E] (AR2025 p.93; PPT Jun 2026).

**Is the FY26 flatness a pause or a peak?** [MC] Management calls it 'a transitional phase' (PPT Jun 2026). [AI] Order intake below sales in FY25 and a weaker Q4 FY26 support the peak reading. The capex announcement and the 96% utilisation claim support the pause reading. Neither side is proven.

**Are the margins structural?** [AI] Bull view: a niche, indigenous product with an engineering-heavy mix supports margins above 30%. [AI] Bear view: FY25 at about 37.8% operating margin followed a mix shift; FY23-FY24 were about 27% (NUMBERS; AR2025 p.84). Management's own word is 'normalisation'.

**Does the market over- or under-price the cash?** [F] The EV in our data is not net of cash (NUMBERS). [AI] About Rs 58 cr of treasury assets at March 2026 makes EV-based multiples look richer than they are. The market may be under-crediting the balance sheet.

**Is the stale DCF misleading in both directions?** [AI] The model starts from FY23 sales of Rs 45.4 cr at a 19% margin (NUMBERS). Company-reported FY26 sales of Rs 72.46 cr already exceed the model's year-2 base-case sales of Rs 65.2 cr. That makes the model conservative on scale and margin. Even so, a price about 4x the bull value still needs growth that the flat FY26 does not show.

**Is the receivable build a collection issue or a timing issue?** [AI] Public-sector and EPC billing tends to be back-ended, and the ageing shows Rs 19.60 cr of the Rs 22.46 cr (March 2025) under six months overdue from the due date (AR2025 p.95). The March 2026 ageing is not available to us.

blocks.text: [AI] The market appears to be paying for the FY25 step-up in scale and margin, with the capacity plan as proof that the step-up continues. Our read of the evidence is narrower. FY25 looks like a year of backlog execution: book-to-bill was about 0.81x [E] (AR2025 p.27). It was followed by flat FY26 sales, lower PAT and a sharp rise in receivables (PPT Jun 2026). The business is clearly profitable, cash-rich and ungeared. What is unproven is the growth. No backlog, order-inflow or customer data is disclosed that would let an investor underwrite the doubling in capacity. The variant view is that the balance sheet makes the downside less severe than the DCF gap implies, while the missing disclosure on orders makes the upside harder to underwrite than the price implies.

summary.one_line: Fluidomat, a debt-free, cash-rich niche maker of fluid couplings, has made a real FY25 step-up to about Rs 72 cr of revenue at margins above 30%, but FY26 was flat, order intake is not visible and receivables are climbing, while the Rs 750 share price sits above every scenario in our FY23-based DCF (reverse DCF about 86% implied growth), so the market is pricing a growth resumption the documents do not yet evidence.
bull_points: [F] Operating profitability has stepped up: PAT rose from Rs 9.61 cr (FY23) to Rs 22.22 cr (FY25) and Rs 20.06 cr (FY26), with operating EBITDA margins of about 33-38% [E] (NUMBERS; AR2025 p.84; PPT Jun 2026).
[F] No borrowings and about Rs 58 cr of FDs, mutual funds and cash at March 2026 [E], which our EV does not net off (PPT Jun 2026; NUMBERS).
[MC] A Rs 35 cr, internally funded expansion lifts capacity from 1,500 to 3,500 units, with existing utilisation at about 96% and eligibility for a 40% capital subsidy (PPT Jun 2026).
[MC] Orders booked on 7 of the 25 thermal and 15 coal-mining projects announced, and a growing position in refinery retrofits at BPCL, IOCL, MRPL and NRL (AR2025 p.36; PPT Jun 2026).
[AI] The DCF is stale: the company already reports EBITDA near the model's bull-case year-5 level, so the model understates current scale and margin (NUMBERS; PPT Jun 2026).
bear_points: [F] FY26 revenue was flat at Rs 72.46 cr and PAT fell to Rs 20.06 cr; Q4 FY26 was weaker than Q4 FY25 on company charts (PPT Jun 2026).
[F] FY25 order booking of Rs 58.16 cr fell 3.1% YoY and was about 0.81x FY25 revenue [E]; no backlog is disclosed (AR2025 p.27).
[E] Debtor days rose from about 89 (FY24) to 149 (FY26); FY25 CFO/PAT was 0.64, with no credit-loss provision on Rs 2.11 cr more than a year overdue (AR2025 p.85, p.95; PPT Jun 2026).
[F] The price of Rs 750 compares with DCF values of Rs 70.9 / 126.5 / 178.4, and the reverse DCF implies about 86% annual sales growth for five years (NUMBERS).

[F] Disclosure is weak: no customer, segment or end-market data; EPS on the P&L includes OCI; CSR figures conflict; the company's EBITDA does not reconcile to its own P&L (AR2025 p.33, p.44, p.84, p.102; PPT Jun 2026).
